entries.c: 零碳产业/能量循环/能量存储/电化学储能/二次电池/锂电池

entries.b:
7 月 2 日消息，在比亚迪今晚的海豹 08 上市发布会上，比亚迪官方宣布，
已累计建成超 7000 座闪充站
，遍布 325 个城市，目标 2026 年底建成 2 万座。
在今年 3 月举行的比亚迪二代刀片电池暨闪充技术发布会上，比亚迪发布了全球量产单枪最大功率充电桩 —— 比亚迪闪充桩，
单枪充电功率可达 1500KW
在使用第二代刀片电池的情况下，比亚迪汽车可以实现 5 分钟电量从 10% 充至 70%，9 分钟充至 97%，刷新充电速度新纪录。IT之家注意到，在零下 30℃ 环境中，比亚迪充电时间仅比常温多 3 分钟（20% 充至 97% 约 12 分钟），打破行业难题。
比亚迪还推出了闪充中国战略，预计到今年年底建成 2 万座闪充站，其中 18000 座闪充站中站、2000 座闪充高速站。

entries.b:
A U.S. aerospace company has unveiled what it says is the world’s first commercial platform that’s capable of testing how hypersonic vehicle materials withstand real weather conditions before ever taking flight.
California-based Auriga Space announced the new capability on Wednesday, July 1, alongside its first client, Axiom Materials, a composite materials manufacturer. The system uses the firm’s Prometheus electromagnetic accelerator that propels test materials through simulated weather.
Axiom Materials will test how advanced materials perform against rain, hail, and airborne particles. The testing is set to close a long-standing gap in hypersonic development. Until now, engineers have depended on limited ground testing or expensive flight tests to evaluate material performance.
Winnie Lai, the founder and CEO of Auriga Space, emphasized the significance of the system. “The hypersonic testing community has badly needed ground truth on material performance for a long time,” she explained.
Hypersonic vehicles travel at speeds of more than
, or five times the speed of sound. This is equal to roughly 3,800 to 15,000 miles per hour (mph). They also experience intense aerodynamic heating and pressure as they travel through the atmosphere.
Even small water droplets or airborne debris can damage the
protective coatings
, radomes, windows, and other critical parts. Auriga’s new chamber is designed to evaluate how materials intended for hypersonic vehicles respond to simulated weather conditions during development.

Instead of sending a full vehicle into the air, the system tests material samples. It propels them through water droplets and other particles at representative flight speeds and pressures. Following the impact, the samples are recovered.
Engineers can then inspect them for damage and measure how they performed. The process enables repeatable testing under realistic weather conditions early in the development cycle. It also reduces uncertainty before full-scale flight tests.
The platform relies on Auriga’s
electromagnetic launch technology
, which uses a magnetically levitated linear electric motor instead of conventional propulsion to accelerate test articles under software-controlled conditions.
As part of the agreement, Axiom Materials will conduct dozens of weather-effects tests within a single week using the Prometheus accelerator. The platform can run more tests than traditional methods under consistent conditions.
Meanwhile, Auriga expects demand for weather testing to grow as investment in hypersonic tech grows. “Making it possible is one big step; making it available at scale is another,” Lai pointed out in a
press statement
. “Auriga’s platform can do both, and that’s exactly what this capability is about.”
At the same time, the Prometheus is already supporting active contracts with the US Air Force and the Missile Defense Agency. According to Auriga, those projects provide a proven foundation for the newly announced commercial capability.
“Allowing our partners at Axiom Materials to accurately
test materials
against realistic conditions will enable the next generation of high-speed systems to be built far faster and flown with confidence,” Lai concluded.
Beyond weather simulation, the reusable, electrically powered electromagnetic launch technology could also support responsive space launch, missile defense, as well as future lunar mass-driver systems.
Correction: An earlier version of this article misstated Auriga Space’s current testing speed. The platform currently operates at Mach 2.5 for materials designed for hypersonic flight, not Mach 5+. The article has been updated accordingly.

entries.b:
Fred Lambert
| Jul 2 2026 - 6:52 am PT
Tesla delivered 480,126 vehicles in the second quarter of 2026, up 25% from the same quarter a year ago and roughly 74,000 vehicles above Wall Street’s consensus estimate.
It’s Tesla’s strongest second quarter ever and its first year-over-year delivery growth after two straight years of decline.
According to Tesla’s
official production and delivery report
, the company produced 451,758 vehicles and delivered 480,126 in Q2 2026.
The bulk came from the high-volume Model 3 and Model Y, which accounted for 442,936 units produced and 467,762 delivered. “Other Models” — Model S, Model X, Cybertruck, and Semi — contributed 8,822 produced and 12,364 delivered.
Here is the full breakdown:
Unlike recent quarters, Tesla delivered more vehicles than it produced, working down about 28,000 units of inventory rather than building it up. That’s a reversal from Q1, when the company
built roughly 50,000 excess vehicles it couldn’t sell
The result marks a clear inflection. Tesla delivered 384,122 vehicles in Q2 2025, so this quarter represents a 25% year-over-year increase — the first quarterly growth the company has posted since its sales peaked in 2023.
It’s also a 34% jump from the 358,023 vehicles Tesla delivered in Q1 2026.
The number blew past expectations. Analysts had
set the consensus at 406,024 deliveries
, with the most bullish estimates from Goldman Sachs and Barclays topping out around 418,000 to 420,000. Tesla beat even the highest forecasts by more than 60,000 units.
At 480,126, the quarter ranks as Tesla’s best-ever Q2, surpassing the 466,140 vehicles it delivered in Q2 2023. It still trails the company’s all-time record of 497,099 deliveries, set in Q3 2025 when US buyers rushed to claim the $7,500 federal EV tax credit before it expired on September 30, 2025.
Tesla also deployed 13.5 GWh of energy storage products in the quarter, up more than 40% from the 9.6 GWh it deployed in Q2 2025.
The energy business has been one of Tesla’s most consistent growth stories, though the Q2 figure came in slightly below the roughly 13.8 GWh analysts had expected.
The delivery surge narrows, but does not close, Tesla’s gap with its biggest rival. BYD
delivered 557,090 fully electric vehicles in Q2 2026
, keeping the Chinese automaker ahead of Tesla in global battery-electric sales.
But the trajectories are moving in opposite directions: BYD’s BEV deliveries fell about 8% year-over-year while Tesla’s jumped 25%. Tesla now sits roughly 77,000 units behind BYD, down from a gap of more than 220,000 units a year ago.
This is a genuinely strong quarter for Tesla, and the data doesn’t leave much room to argue otherwise. A 25% year-over-year jump, an 18% beat over consensus, more deliveries than production, and the best Q2 in company history — after two years of shrinking sales, that’s a real inflection, not a rounding error.
The obvious question is what’s driving it. The gas prices are the obvious answer.
The war in Iran has created a significant surge in gas prices, which has now stopped, but it resulted a massive increase in demand for EVs while Tesla was sitting on 50,000 extra vehicles from last quarter.
